title: Caching in Nodics
readerIntent: Understand how Nodics improves response time without making cache authoritative.
priorKnowledge: Understand the owning source of data.
owner: Nodics provider-neutral cache capability and configured cache adapters
summary: Cache channels define tenant-safe keys, eligibility, TTL, invalidation, fallback, and provider requirements while authoritative data remains recoverable from its owner.

sections.heading: Business outcomes
items: Reduce repeated database, search, API, configuration, and computation work.
Select local or distributed behavior per channel and topology.
Change TTL and provider through layered configuration.
Fail safely when a provider cannot meet security or consistency requirements.

sections.heading: Core rule
paragraphs: A cache is a temporary projection. Every entry needs an owner, source fallback, bounded key, isolation scope, TTL, invalidation trigger, acceptable staleness, outage rule, diagnostics, and tests.
